units.text: Your birthday opens a new year today. Read your year.
A different season of your life begins this year. Read your year.
units.note: YR-6 proposal kept 'today' as the exact start, which the owner rule bars. Says 'this year' instead, and avoids 'ten-year' because the headline now carries it.

units.text: The next ten years of your life take shape this year. Read your year.
units.note: R2-18 proposal said 'begins today', which claims an exact start. No 'gate', no 'today'.

units.text: The month changes today. Read your month.
The new year opens today. Read your year.
Today starts your next year of age. You carry the last one into it, what it taught you and what it cost.
Your next long cycle begins around this birthday and runs until the following one takes over. The years inside it each read against this new backdrop for you.
units.note: YR-7 applied: 'around this birthday', no 'luck'. 'ten-year' left to the headline so the word does not repeat on the page.

units.text: Around this time of year, one ten-year stretch of your life gives way to the next. A fresh part of you comes into its own, carrying the years behind you.
units.note: No finding on the text itself, but it claimed 'this birthday' as the exact start of the ten-year stage, which the owner rule bars.

units.text: The solar month turns today, and a different energy takes over from the last. The first days show which of your habits still suit the change.
units.note: R1-m7 proposal still said 'new month'. Reworded so the page does not say it three times.

units.text: A new year opens today, and its energy runs until next February. The turn reaches you before you can name it.
Today repeats your birth day in the sixty-day count, as it does six times a year. What you began two months back comes up for a second look.
units.note: R1-m4 proposal ran 32 words; trimmed to 28.

units.text: Today turns your own day over, its stem against yours and its branch striking your Day Gate. A settled matter at home is questioned, and the answering falls to you.
Attraction is strong today, and people notice you more than usual. Glances and easy talk find you, along with attention you did not ask for.
Tense moments today arrive with less weight, and harsh words land more gently. That lasts only while you keep your own tone mild.
units.note: R2-15 proposal kept 'The day asks little of your nerves', which names no cost or condition (AP4). Close now names a condition.

units.text: Help comes from someone with standing, an elder or a near stranger who owes you nothing. The price is your pride, which you set aside to accept it.
units.note: Gerund-it-cost frame (R1-M3) recast with the cost as subject.

units.text: The day moves you, with travel, an errand across town or a change of place. Your plans stretch to fit the distance.
A setback today carries something useful inside it. Reaching it takes your work, not luck.
Plans at home change suddenly today. Read your day.
A settled plan at work comes loose today. Read your day.
Something in your first home shifts today. Read your day.
An old friction at home returns today. Read your day.
The same complaint at work returns today. Read your day.
An old family argument resurfaces today. Read your day.
an older relative's remark hurts
units.note: R1-m1 proposal 'lands wrong' repeats the landing's own words, and 'stings' is spent by harm.day.

units.text: The day you were born on repeats today. Read your day.
units.note: R1-m6 applied in new wording, so it does not open like the pillar line ('Today repeats your').

units.text: Something settled at home gets questioned today. Read your day.
{el} makes you dig in
a home matter gathers force
units.note: Takes YR-3 (no settled outcome); 'pulls together' and 'pulls the same way' read as a result and echo the landing.

units.text: Under it runs {g}, which the {e} shapes. The two bear down on you as one steady pressure.
Under it runs {g}, which the {e} feeds. Part of its force drains away before it gets to you.
Under it runs more {g}. You take it at full strength.
Under it runs {g}, which feeds the {e}. It keeps that energy strong on you from start to finish.
units.note: R2-05 proposal said 'from morning to night', which is wrong on month and year pages.

units.text: a work alliance takes shape
units.note: Neither 'deal' (absent from the day landing) nor 'a stalled task moves' (settles it) fits both pages; this names what arrives.

units.text: a long plan loops back
the day's edges soften
units.note: R2-15 proposal repeated the star line's words on the same page.

units.text: a hard turn has its uses
units.note: R2-16 proposal repeated the star line ('A setback ... something useful').

units.text: Something you set for later shifts today. Read your day.
Your best pitch|a cautious suggestion
A decision made on time|endless review
An old sticking point with someone younger returns. Read your day.
Unhurried meals at the table|eating on the run
Splitting the housework|doing it all
a new ten-year chapter starts
Clearing a backlog|a fresh brief
